identification: Late Victorian full-calf gilt-ruled ledger/album (blind and gilt fillet panels, corner fleurons, raised-band spine with fleurons, no title) with an alphabet thumb index (coloured A-Z tabs), used as a family commonplace book: neat manuscript entries including 'Gooseberry Fool' recipe, a list of parlour 'Games' (Blind Man's Buff, Twenty Questions, Geography etc.), and a 'Gun Powder' trial note dated Sept 1884 comparing Curtis & Harvey's Diamond Grain black powder with a 'White Powder' (penetration of 56 pages of a book by 7 shots), plus 'Gallo Gal...' recipe. Loose with it: a handwritten letter on blue squared paper, a pencil sketch of figures with a horse/animals in a landscape (unsigned as far as visible), a blue printed legal-looking form beginning 'Her Majesty' / 'Greeting' (writ or commission, Victorian era) and blue manuscript sheets with an envelope bearing a single red stamp and circular postmarks. Origin (English or colonial) not determinable from the photos.

viewing_check: Flyleaf, pastedowns and first pages for an owner's name, house or town; dates and places in the loose letter on blue squared paper; what the blue printed 'Her Majesty ... Greeting' form is (writ, commission or summons) and where issued; read the stamp and postmarks on the envelope (a colonial Tasmanian or Victorian cover could be worth more than the book); signature on the pencil sketch; how many pages are filled. Buy only if a Tasmanian name or place turns up, and then cheaply.
